transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-07
Time: 14:00 PT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Lin (Redwood AE), Marcus Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Sharma (Crestwell Head of Data), Ethan Cole (Platform Eng), Dr. Maria Gomez (Clinical Lead)

Summary:
- POC length: 4 weeks (business-facing evaluation + technical benchmark).
- Goal: validate quality for clinical summarization & triage assistant workflows; define golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, and scoring approach.
- Success criteria: format/structure pass rate >= 95%, hallucination rate < 5% on sampled outputs, end-to-end latency within target (95p < 350ms hosted; goal <200ms on dedicated), and human review score >= 4.0/5 on 10% sample.

Topics discussed:
1) Workload sizing and token profile
2) Benchmark plan: latency, throughput, cost, quality
3) Quality eval plan details: golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination detection, scoring rubric
4) Timelines and next steps + compliance docs

Action items (recap):
- Jamie to send SOW/pricing and POC runbook.
- Marcus to run preliminary perf tests and share config.
- Priya to drop sample prompts and expected outputs (500).
- Ethan to confirm VPC/network/firewall constraints.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: hey everyone thanks for joining, I think we have about an hour,quick intros?
[00:12] Priya: Priya here, head of data at Crestwell. i'll focus on the evaluation criteria and the sample data side.
[00:18] Ethan: Ethan, platform eng, i'll handle network and infra constraints.
[00:23] Dr. Gomez: Maria, clinical lead, i'll be reviewing outputs for safety and hallucinations.
[00:29] Marcus: Marcus from Redwood SE, i'll handle benchmarks and toks sorry tokenization—bench config.
[00:35] Jamie: cool, we sent a short pre-read, today's goal is to align on success criteria and the quality eval plan for the 4 week POC.

[02:10] Priya: high level — two main workflows: clinical note summarization (longer input, expected concise structured output) and triage assistant (question/answer + suggested next steps). average input length is around 400–700 tokens, outputs 60–180 tokens, about 5–10k requests per day in pilot, spike 50 rps.

[03:05] Marcus: ok that maps to a modest sizing. for the benchmark we want to capture 95th percentile latency, p50/p95 token latency, and cost per 1M tokens. if you expect spikes to 50 rps we'll emulate 2x spike during bench.

[04:12] Priya: accuracy metrics — for summarization we use exact-match on critical fields (diagnosis, meds) and ROUGE/ROUGE-L as a loose metric. for the triage assistant we prefer intent accuracy plus human graded relevance (1–5).

[05:20] Dr. Gomez: hallucination is the biggest clinical risk. we need an automated detector plus human spot checks. anything that invents treatments or dosages must be caught. target <5% hallucination on sampled responses.

[06:04] Jamie: on Redwood side we'll propose a quality eval plan with: golden prompts (canonical examples), regression tests (old vs new model), hallucination/format checks (schema validators + heuristics), and a combined scoring approach — mix of automated and human scoring.

[07:12] Ethan: question — network: we need to know if this will be hosted (Redwood API) or dedicated/private. we have strict egress policies and can't allow data to hit public internet unless under BAA and encryption.

[07:40] Jamie: understood — for POC we can do hosted with appropriate data handling (PII scrubbing) or bring a private deployment. we'll include both runbooks. we also shared our compliance pack in drive.

[09:05] Marcus: diving into the quality eval specifics: first, golden prompts. Priya, can you confirm you'll provide ~50 canonical prompts per workflow with expected outputs? these become our "golden" set for automated checks.
[09:28] Priya: yes we can do 50 each initially, we can supply expected fields and preferred phrasing for structured output.

[10:01] Marcus: great. automation: we'll run exact-match checks for structured fields, regex/JSON schema validation for format, and fuzzy metrics (ROUGE / token-level F1) for free-text. then flagged items go into a human-review queue.

[12:15] Dr. Gomez: human review scope? i propose 10% random sample + all flagged hallucination candidates. reviewers will rate relevance and safety 1–5.

[13:20] Jamie: recommended scoring: Weighted score = 0.6 * automated score + 0.4 * human score. automated score itself is composite: 50% schema/format pass rate, 50% quality metric (ROUGE/exact-match).

[14:10] Ethan: for regression tests, do we run new model vs baseline?
[14:18] Marcus: yes. baseline will be your current system (if any) or a stable open model (we suggested Redwood-verified m-2 in pre-read). regression harness will run golden set + 5k random sample.

[15:45] Priya: how do we detect hallucinations automatically?
[15:53] Marcus: heuristics include presence of names/dates that are inconsistent, out-of-scope entity detection, contradiction with input (we run an entailment check), and domain-specific triggers (e.g., new drug names not in formulary). we'll return a hallucination score per output; anything > threshold mvt into manual review. note detection is imperfect.

[17:40] Dr. Gomez: entailment checks sound good; please ensure we can configure the formulary whitelist and banned assertion list.

[19:10] Jamie: format checks: if the output is expected JSON with fields diagnosis, summary, next_steps, then we'd run a schema validator. format fail counts heavily against automated score. target schema pass >= 95%.

[21:00] Marcus: benchmarks — we'll run: single-request latency (p50/p95), throughput sweep to target 50 rps with increasing concurrency, cold-start behavior, and cost per 1M tokens. we'll attach the exact benchmark script.

[22:30] Priya: are you going to test with quantized models? we may be interested in cost/quality tradeoffs.
[22:40] Marcus: yes, we'll test at least two model variants: a higher-quality full model and a quantized reduced-cost variant. we'll include model/quantization recommendations in the POC report.

[24:10] Ethan: timeline — what's realistic for data prep and runs?
[24:20] Jamie: week 0 (this week) — confirm SOW + security pack; week 1 — ingest prompts & data and run golden-set smoke tests; week 2 — perf benchmark and regression runs; week 3 — human evaluation sampling and follow-ups; week 4 — POC report + wrap. so 4 weeks end-to-end.

[25:55] Priya: marker for success — if weighted score >= 0.85 (on 0–1 normalized) and hallucination <5% we'll consider quality validated. plus latency SLOs met.

[27:30] Marcus: example scoring breakdown in practice: for one example: schema pass (1 or 0), exact-match score 0.9, rouge 0.72 -> automated composite ~0.86; human mean 4.3/5 -> normalized 0.86; weighted = .6*.86 + .4*.86 ~ .86.

[29:00] Dr. Gomez: remind me about logging/audit — we need redaction and audit logs for clinician review.

[29:12] Jamie: Redwood provides request/response logs with pii redaction capability and audit trails in console. we'll include the retention and export options.

[31:40] Ethan: connectivity — if we go hosted we'll need IP allowlist and BAA. Priya, can you confirm whether data can be pseudonymized before egress?

[32:00] Priya: yes we can pseudonymize patient identifiers for the POC; for final production we'll need a private deployment or BAA constraints.

[34:10] Marcus: on hallucination tooling we'll surface a hallucination reason code (entailment-fail, invents-entity, out-of-knowledge) to help triage.

[35:55] Dr. Gomez: good. also want a format check specifically to ensure drug dosages are never invented; we want an explicit fail policy if the model asserts dosage changes.

[37:10] Jamie: noted — we will include rules to escalate any dosage-related assertions to immediate manual review and include an automatic block in the scoring pipeline.

[39:30] Priya: what about regression cadence? if we iterate models weekly how do we avoid quality regressions?

[39:45] Marcus: the regression harness runs nightly during the POC against the golden set and pushes any regression > delta threshold to a Slack webhook + backlog. we can set thresholds (e.g., >3% drop in automated score).

[41:12] Ethan: expected deliverables at end: POC report with perf results, quality summary, recommended model/quant setting, and a suggested production rollout plan.

[41:40] Jamie: yes deliverables: 1) Benchmark report, 2) Quality eval report (detailed per prompt), 3) POC recommendations and cost table, 4) Runbook for production deployment (hosted/dedicated/private).

[44:05] Priya: for the human review process we want to use clinicians internally but could use Redwood's support for annotation tooling if needed.

[44:35] Marcus: we'll provide a simple annotation UI and CSV outputs; if you want Redwood-managed human labeling we can discuss as an add-on.

[46:10] Dr. Gomez: timeline for human review throughput — how many samples can you process?

[46:18] Marcus: for the POC we plan to do 10% sampling of ~5k outputs = 500 human reviews. Redwood tooling+your clinicians should complete in about 3–4 days with batching.

[48:00] Priya: ok that's doable. next, reporting: we want a dashboard with per-prompt fail rates and hallucination alerts.

[48:12] Jamie: Redwood Console will show per-route/model dashboards and we can add a per-prompt table via exported CSV/BI.

[49:50] Ethan: any blockers for starting next week?

[50:00] Jamie: blockers: we need sample prompts/data, confirmation on hosted vs dedicated for the POC, and SOW sign-off. once we have those, Marcus can schedule benchmark runs.

[51:20] Priya: we'll upload the sample set by Friday (2026-09-11) and confirm pseudonymization.

[52:00] Marcus: i'll prepare the perf harness and share the exact JMeter/bench config and the model variants we'll test (full vs quantized).

[53:40] Dr. Gomez: on scoring, i'd like an additional clinical safety pass where any output tagged as high-risk is flagged and shown to clinician within 2 hours.

[54:00] Jamie: we can add an alerting rule and escalation path in the POC runbook.

[55:30] Ethan: security docs — we'll need SOC2, ISO, encryption at rest, KMS integration notes.

[55:50] Jamie: got it, we'll attach the security pack in the shared drive and send a separate email.

[57:05] Priya: final question — pricing for POC and pilot?

[57:14] Jamie: we'll include a POC pricing line (fixed amount to cover dedicated benchmark capacity and Redwood engineering time) and example consumption costs for hosted; detailed numbers go into the SOW.

[59:00] Marcus: quick recap of success criteria: weighted quality score >= 0.85, hallucination <5% on sampled, schema pass >=95%, latency SLOs met.

[60:05] Priya: agreed. we'll aim to sign SOW quick so we can start.

[61:00] Jamie: great thanks everyone, we'll send notes and the SOW + security pack by Thursday. next meeting — alignment after initial benchmarks (week of 2026-09-14).

[61:30] Ethan: thanks all.
[61:35] Dr. Gomez: thanks.

End of transcript.
